rationale: The recursion at structural_rules.py:281 exists solely to cross-validate with: bindings against the child's parameters. Its except Exception: continue already swallows child ERRORs, so propagating child WARNINGs would surface the mild findings while the severe ones stay silent. ValidationError also has no provenance field, so a propagated child violation would be recorded as the parent's - replacing one misattribution with another. Per-loop scope coverage is already enforced independently by ll-doctor's _loop_validity_data and TestValidatorWarningBudget, which iterate every loop file directly, so nothing is lost by suppression.
rule: Recursive load_and_validate() calls into child loops pass raise_on_error=False and discard the returned violations. A loop's validation reports only that loop's own findings; a child's warnings are reported when the child is itself validated.
alternatives_rejected: Option B (propagate): fold child warnings into the parent's returned errors list so they reach --json violations. Rejected - it would require adding a source-loop field to ValidationError and threading it through every rule and consumer, would give every parent loop referencing one of the 11 unscoped loops/oracles/*.yaml new violations entries, would shift TestValidatorWarningBudget, and could flip workflow-generator.yaml's baseline/candidate regression gate for reasons unrelated to the artifact under test. Only viable bundled with a scope backfill across those 11 oracles.
